Clause (iii)'s content is right in Lean, as before: the bounded quantity is F_slow(U^[N]) of (5.24), the exponent 2Nh-2-M is 2h(N+1)-K_m with K_m = 2h+2+m independent of N, and the axis is included (lo = 0). Clauses (i) and (ii) are each one instantiation away from stated declarations. The earlier DELTA rested on the quantifier of (5.25), and that ground does not hold up.

What one declaration states. finite_error_rate (BaseResidual.lean:2477) gives the bound only eventually along a filter whose scale tends to 0. No declaration states it for every 0 < q <= 1, and none of the three theorems taking a PhysicalApproach can be instantiated at a filter on which q is bounded below.

What follows by combination. I opened the three proof bodies. They use the PhysicalApproach only through its carrier, in_carrier, past and radial fields and through positive_small (363-367), which takes from scale nothing but q <= 1. No limit or smallness threshold appears in the chain. The estimate underneath, cartesian_finite_monomials_bound (314), is already in set form for every q <= 1. It rests on homogeneous_derivative_bound (PhysicalCoordinateBounds.lean:312), which rescales to q = 1 and uses compactness in (X, eta). The assembly lemmas are stated for an arbitrary filter, and the identification with the true residual (regularTruncation_eq, FiniteIdentities, eqOn_of_off_axis) is pointwise with no condition on q. So on S = B ∩ {t<1} ∩ {q<=1} ∩ {X in Icc lo hi} the same three proofs (53 lines) go through at the principal filter of S and give one constant on all of S. in_compact_of_radial_bound (WholeDomainPhysicalCompact.lean:27) supplies B = closedBall 0 (X_max+2) for the paper's range. This is a combination of stated declarations with no new analytic fact. It is a re-proof of three lemmas, not an instantiation, and I read it without compiling it.

Where the two Lean traces differ, the adversarial account of the mechanism is the accurate one. The earlier reason, "compactness plus continuity of the jets on delta <= q <= 1", is not how the range is closed and would not work as stated: by (3.2) on p. 7 that region reaches t = 1 as |eta| -> 1, where the Lean has no smoothness statements. The scaling lemma closes it instead.

What the paper needs. (5.33) on p. 57 is worded as uniform over the full domain, so the earlier reading of the wording was right. The proof of Lemma 5.4 uses it only after shrinking the q-neighbourhood (p. 59, Step 3), its conclusion (5.36) is for 0 < q < delta (p. 58), and Proposition 5.5 is stated as q decreases to 0 (p. 60). The small-q uniform form is what finite_error_rate gives directly.

Hence different_formulation and SINGLE_SOURCE_OK. The q-range finding stays as a low attribution gap: the printed range is not stated by any declaration, and the full-range bound for the constructed sequence is not stated in either form.

Not graded here: every Lean statement in this chain requires t < 1, which is |eta| < 1. The paper's closed range -1 <= eta <= 1 includes eta = ±1, which are points at t = 1 away from the singular point (p. 7). Those are reached only as one-sided limits, in the filter form and in the derived form alike.

Not re-derived in this re-check: that residual minus prefixStressForce is F_slow, the exponent match, and that the Lean coefficient sequence is the paper's. These are carried over from the item ruling.

findings.summary: No single declaration states (5.25) on all of 0 < q <= 1: finite_error_rate states it only eventually along filters with q -> 0. The full-range bound does follow from stated declarations with no new analytic fact, by re-running three filter proofs (53 lines) at a principal filter; I read that derivation and did not compile it.

No declaration states Proposition 5.3. Its three clauses live in three files: the order-by-order construction in GlobalSlowProfiles, divergence-freeness in AxisymmetricFields/SpatialCurl, and the residual estimate in BaseResidual.
Clause (ii) is stated for the finite sum, but only off the axis, and in a different file from clause (iii) under a different name for the same field. Reaching the axis needs the separate curl route.

The paper's seminorm is the max of mixed space-time partials of order ≤ m; the Lean bounds the full iterated Fréchet derivative norm in the joint variable. The Lean norm dominates every such partial, so this costs nothing.

No declaration states (5.25) for the constructed sequence: finite_error_rate is generic in the coefficients d and profiles f and carries their hypotheses. They are discharged unconditionally for the realized base elsewhere, so the statement is not vacuous.

The paper applies Lemma 5.1 afresh at each order; the Lean Scheme fixes the whole family of near-axis seeds in advance and the recursion repairs only the annulus a ≤ R ≤ b, coupling to the lower orders through the moment rows.
